formats.key: SafeTx(address to,uint256 value,bytes data,uint8 operation,uint256 safeTxGas,uint256 baseGas,uint256 gasPrice,address gasToken,address refundReceiver,uint256 nonce)
effects: With operation 0 (Call), the Safe sends `value` native currency to `to` and calls it with `data`; the Safe is msg.sender of that call.

With operation 1 (Delegate Call), the Safe runs the code of `to` in its own context. `value` is not sent, and that code can move any asset of the Safe or change its owners, modules, guard or fallback handler.

When gasPrice > 0, the Safe pays a gas refund of (gasUsed + baseGas) * min(gasPrice, tx.gasprice) in ETH, or (gasUsed + baseGas) * gasPrice in gasToken. The refund goes to refundReceiver, or to tx.origin when refundReceiver is the zero address.
When gasPrice > 0, the inner call gets only safeTxGas gas. If the inner call fails, the Safe still pays the refund and the nonce is still used.
The signature counts toward the Safe threshold for this nonce. Executing the transaction uses up the nonce.
formats.shown: The intent "Safe", then To, Value (ETH), Operation type (Call / Delegate Call), the nested call decoded against `to`, and raw baseGas, gasPrice, gasToken and refundReceiver; safeTxGas and nonce are hidden.

findings.title: SafeTx decodes the nested data as a call to `to` with `value`, also when the operation is a delegate call.
findings.evidence: Executor.execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }`, which sends no value and runs `to`'s code in the Safe. Descriptor field `data`: format "calldata", params {"calleePath": "to", "amountPath": "value", "spenderPath": "@.to"}, with no condition on `operation`. When operation is 1, the nested screen describes a call to `to` that does not happen, and `Value` shows ETH that does not move.
findings.fix: Show the nested call as decoded calldata only when operation is 0 (Call). When operation is 1, show `data` as raw bytes with a warning label, such as "Delegate call: code runs with all Safe assets". Add a delegate-call test case.

findings.title: SafeTx intent "Safe" does not say that the Safe executes a transaction or moves funds.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "intent": "Safe", with no interpolatedIntent. Safe.execTransaction runs execute(to, value, data, operation, ...) and can pay a gas refund.
findings.fix: Set "intent": "Execute Safe transaction" and "interpolatedIntent": "Execute {operation} to {to} with {value}".

findings.title: SafeTx shows the gas refund parameters as raw numbers and addresses, with no token or total.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice)`, paid in `gasToken` (the zero address means ETH). Descriptor fields: baseGas 'Gas amount' (raw), gasPrice 'Gas price' (raw), gasToken 'Gas token' (raw). baseGas is the extra gas added to gasUsed, not the total gas amount.
findings.fix: Format gasPrice as tokenAmount with tokenPath "gasToken" and nativeCurrencyAddress set to the zero address. Show gasToken as addressName or token. Rename baseGas to "Base gas (added to refund)".

findings.title: SafeTx shows a zero refundReceiver as 0x000…, but the code then pays the refund to tx.origin.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `address payable receiver = refundReceiver == address(0) ? payable(tx.origin) : refundReceiver;`. Descriptor: refundReceiver 'Gas receiver' (raw). Case 0 shows 'Gas receiver: 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000'.
findings.fix: Use format addressName for refundReceiver. Add a label or message that says a zero address means the refund goes to the transaction executor.

findings.title: SafeTx hides safeTxGas, which limits the gas and refund of the inner call and decides whether a failed call still costs a refund.
findings.evidence: Safe.execTransaction: `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, gasPrice == 0 ? (gasleft() - 2500) : safeTxGas);` and `if (gasPrice > 0) { payment = handlePayment(gasUsed, ...) }`. The refund is paid even when the call fails. Descriptor: {"label": "Safe Tx Gas", "path": "safeTxGas", "visible": "never"}.
findings.fix: Make safeTxGas visible, at least when gasPrice is not 0, with format raw and the label "Inner call gas limit".

findings.title: SafeTx binds only to the SafeL2 singleton, but real SafeTx messages use each Safe proxy as verifyingContract.
findings.evidence: Safe.sol: DOMAIN_SEPARATOR_TYPEHASH is 'EIP712Domain(uint256 chainId,address verifyingContract)', and the domain uses address(this), which is the proxy. meta.json: 0xedd160… is 'contracts/SafeL2.sol:SafeL2'. The constructor sets threshold = 1 with no owners ('an unusable Safe'). Descriptor deployments list only 0xEdd160fEBBD92E350D4D398fb636302fccd67C7e on every chain.
findings.fix: Bind the descriptor to Safe proxies that use this singleton, with a factory constraint on SafeProxyFactory's ProxyCreation event, not to the singleton address.

findings.title: SafeTx has one test case: a plain ETH call with no gas refund, no delegate call and no nested calldata.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: operation 0, data '0x', gasPrice '0', refundReceiver zero. No case covers operation 1, gasPrice > 0 with a gasToken, or nested calldata that should be decoded.
findings.fix: Add cases for a delegate call, an ERC-20 transfer as nested calldata, and a refund paid in an ERC-20 gasToken.

findings.title: SafeTx refund total depends on gasUsed at execution time, so no field can show the exact amount.
findings.evidence: Safe.handlePayment: `payment = gasUsed.add(baseGas).mul(gasPrice < tx.gasprice ? gasPrice : tx.gasprice)`. gasUsed is measured during execution and is not in the message.

findings.title: SafeTx decodes the nested data as a call to `to` with `value`, also when the operation is a delegate call.
findings.reason: When operation is 1, the Safe runs `to`'s code in its own account with its own balances and sends no value. The nested screen still describes a normal call to `to` that carries `value`, which is not what happens. The 'Operation type' enum row does show 'Delegate Call', but prompt.md's calibrated criticals cover this exact case: 'Embedded calldata is decoded as a call to `to` while `operation` can make it a delegate call', because the nested display states an outcome that does not occur.
findings.quote: Executor.sol execute: `success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0)` (operation == DelegateCall), reached from Safe.sol execTransaction `success = execute(to, value, data, operation, ...)`. Nothing restricts `operation`. descriptor.json SafeTx field `data`: {"format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"}}, with no condition on `operation`.

findings.format: SafeTx(address to,uint256 value,bytes data,uint8 operation,uint256 safeTxGas,uint256 baseGas,uint256 gasPrice,address gasToken,address refundReceiver,uint256 nonce)
findings.title: SafeTx decodes the nested data as a call to `to` with `value`, also when the operation is a delegate call.
findings.reason: The always-visible “Delegate Call” enum discloses the operation, but does not correct the nested decoder’s unconditional use of `value` as transferred ETH. The delegatecall branch ignores that value and executes in the Safe’s context, matching the guide’s explicit critical example.
findings.quote: contracts/1-0xedd160febbd92e350d4d398fb636302fccd67c7e/src/contracts/base/Executor.sol, execute: `if (operation == Enum.Operation.DelegateCall) { ... success := delegatecall(txGas, to, add(data, 0x20), mload(data), 0, 0) }`. descriptor.json, SafeTx: `{"path":"value","label":"Value","format":"amount","visible":"always"}` and `{"path":"data","label":"Transaction","format":"calldata","params":{"calleePath":"to","amountPath":"value","spenderPath":"@.to"},"visible":"always"}`. Registry .github/scripts/ai-review/prompt.md, examples: “Embedded calldata is decoded as a call to `to` while `operation` can make it a delegate call that runs `to`'s code in the signer's account”.
